longTerm.title: Long-term ranking: quality + value + momentum
longTerm.shortDescription: Relative score 0–100 for a 1–3 year research horizon; not a probability of growth or a forecast return.

freshness.label: Data status
freshness.stale: Reload failed. Showing the last successfully loaded results; they may be out of date.
freshness.explanation: Dates cover the whole selected market. Last loaded is when this page received the ranking; financial observation dates are when StockPilot received the figures, not their publication dates.
freshness.issues: Financial inputs: {{missing}} stocks missing data or an observation date; {{stale}} flagged as stale.

chart.title: Recorded scores over time
chart.description: The timeline shows when each score was recorded. Every point is a stored observation; missing scores and model changes break the line. Same-day revisions are preserved.
chart.insufficient: The chart needs scores recorded at two or more distinct times. Existing records are available below.
chart.overlapping: Some records share an identical timestamp and may overlap on the chart. Every revision is available below.
chart.invalidDates: Records without a valid observation time are omitted from the chart and remain in the list below.

longTerm.description: A research ranking for a 1–3 year horizon. The 0–100 score compares stocks with their peers; it is not a probability of growth or a forecast return. Long-term performance has not yet been validated.
longTerm.methodology: Initial heuristic: each of the three factors has equal weight (⅓). A higher score means stronger inputs relative to the comparison group, not guaranteed returns.
longTerm.coverageExplanation: Coverage is the share of the six inputs available. A complete score also requires fresh data, enough comparable stocks, and liquidity and size checks. A dash means the stock could not be scored, not zero.

explanations.quality: Return on equity, return on assets and net profit margin describe profitability.
explanations.value: Earnings yield (earnings / price, the inverse of P/E) compares earnings with the share price.
explanations.momentum: Price changes over 12 and 6 months, excluding the most recent month. This describes the past trend.

longTerm.noneScored: No stock has enough valid inputs and comparable peers for a complete score yet.
longTerm.empty: No ranking data yet. Observations will appear after a successful data refresh.
longTerm.noMatches: No company matches these filters. Try clearing them or add stocks to your watchlist.
longTerm.comparison: Financial comparison group: {{group}}. Momentum compares stocks across the market. Minimum comparison group size, including this stock: {{peers}}.

groups.mixed: sector or market, depending on the metric

longTerm.lossValuationInput: The model uses a zero E/P input for known zero or negative net income or earnings per share. This is a scoring rule, not an observed 0% earnings yield.
longTerm.quarterlyCurrencyContext: Reporting currency at observation: {{currency}}. Currency was not archived separately for these report periods.
longTerm.historyExplanation: History starts when StockPilot records an observation. Observation time is when the system received the figures; it is not their original publication date. The market session and financial report period are shown separately. A revised report is kept as another observation, without changing earlier entries.

longTerm.noFinancialHistory: No financial observations yet. Recording begins with a successful financial data refresh.
longTerm.noPeriods: This observation contains no report periods.
longTerm.latestScores: Showing up to 100 latest score records, newest first.

overview.heading: Market overview
overview.breadthInfo: How the ranked stocks split by verdict, plus simple counts: stocks that rose or fell in the latest session, stocks whose VSA rating rose or fell since the previous session, and new 52-week highs and lows. These are counts, not a forecast — they say how many stocks lean each way, not whether the move is early or late.
overview.splitAria: {{bullish}}% of stocks are Buy or Strong Buy, {{bearish}}% are Sell or Strong Sell.
overview.risersInfo: The stocks whose VSA rating rose the most in the latest session (rating before → after). A rising rating means the latest bar changed the volume-and-spread reading in the stock's favour; it is not a price target.
overview.fallersInfo: The stocks whose VSA rating fell the most in the latest session (rating before → after).
overview.noMovers: No stock changed its rating in the latest session.

columns.heading: Show columns

info.priceChangePct: The latest session’s price change, percent. While the exchange is open it is today’s change so far (the price then carries a blue dot).
info.dist52wHigh: How far below the 52-week high the last close sits. 0% means it closed at the high; a “NEW” chip marks a session that set a fresh 52-week high.
info.dist52wLow: How far above the 52-week low the last close sits. A “NEW” chip marks a session that set a fresh 52-week low.
info.rating: VSA score with time decay: recent bullish signals push it above 50, bearish ones below. Green above 70 (strong accumulation), red below 30 (distribution).
info.ratingChange: Change in the VSA rating versus the previous session — the day-over-day mover.
info.signal: Verdict from the most recent VSA pattern: Spring / SOS → Strong Buy, Successful Test → Buy, No Demand → Sell, Upthrust / SOW → Strong Sell. No recent pattern → Hold.
info.daysSinceSignal: Sessions since the last VSA pattern fired. Fresh signals matter most in VSA — old ones fade.
info.volume: 20-session median daily volume, in shares — a liquidity gauge.
info.aiConfidence: Confidence of the built-in AI-insight engine in its verdict, 0–100.
info.trend: Recent price path over the analysis window.

columns.reorderHint: Tick the columns to show; use the arrows to change their order in the table.

weekly.label: 1W
weekly.confirmsInfo: Weekly VSA agrees with the daily signal — the weekly chart reads {{verdict}} ({{rating}}/100). Higher-timeframe confirmation.
weekly.conflictsInfo: Weekly VSA contradicts the daily signal — the weekly chart reads {{verdict}} ({{rating}}/100). Treat the daily call with caution.
weekly.filterInfo: Only stocks whose weekly VSA verdict leans the same way as the daily one (both bullish, or both bearish). Weekly candles are the stored daily bars resampled to weeks and run through the same VSA engine.
weekly.columnInfo: The same VSA engine run on weekly candles. Blank when the stock has under ~30 weeks of stored history.

chart.noIntradayBody: Yahoo Finance does not publish intraday candles for every listing. Pick 1D or 1W above — the daily and weekly charts, and everything else on this page, are unaffected.
chart.intervalHint: Bar size: 30m, 1H and 4H are intraday; 1D and 1W are end-of-day
chart.intradayNote: Intraday {{interval}} candles are fetched live and reach back to {{from}}; the rating above and the trading-method overlays stay on daily bars.
chart.timeRangeHint: Scroll or zoom the chart to change the range automatically

fundamentals.title: Fundamentals
fundamentals.info: Company fundamentals from Yahoo Finance, refreshed daily. Market cap = market value of all shares; P/E = price divided by yearly earnings per share (lower can mean cheaper); EPS = earnings per share; Dividend yield = yearly dividend as % of the price.
fundamentals.priceReturnInfo: How much the share price alone moved over each period, measured from this stock's own stored price history. Dividends are NOT included, so for a high-yielding stock your actual return was higher. “—” means the stored history doesn't reach back that far yet.
fundamentals.incomeInfo: Revenue and profit over the last four reported quarters (trailing 12 months). ROE = profit earned per zloty of shareholder capital; ROA = profit per zloty of assets — higher generally means a more efficient business. “—” means the figure was not reported.
fundamentals.investmentInfo: Money the company spends on its own business — factories, machines, buildings, software. “% of revenue” shows how capital-intensive it is; “% of cash flow” above 100% means it invests more than the business itself generates, so the rest comes from reserves or debt. Compare companies on the Investment page.
fundamentals.noInvestmentData: No investment data reported for this company.

rating.title: VSA Rating
rating.info: 0–100 score built from all detected VSA signals with time decay: recent signals count more, old ones fade out (half impact after ~30 days). Above 70 = strong accumulation (green), around 50 = neutral, below 30 = distribution (red).
rating.weeklyInfo: The same VSA engine run on weekly candles — the stored daily bars resampled into weeks, over the last 52 weeks. VSA traders trust a daily signal far more when the higher timeframe tells the same story. Independent of the chart's bar size: this is always the weekly read of the stock.
rating.weeklyUnavailable: Not enough history — a weekly read needs about 30 weeks of stored daily bars.

agreement.confirms: The weekly chart confirms the daily signal — both lean the same way.
agreement.conflicts: The weekly chart contradicts the daily signal — treat the daily call with caution.
agreement.neutral: The weekly chart is neutral — it neither backs nor contradicts the daily signal.

methods.toggle: Show or hide {{name}} markers on the chart
methods.positiveHint: A green label or arrow is a bullish signal: the method reads strength on this bar.
methods.negativeHint: A red label or arrow is a bearish signal: the method reads weakness on this bar — a warning.
methods.watchHint: A grey label beside a small square is a pattern the method looked at and refused; the label says why. Neither a buy nor a sell.
methods.dotIsMethodHint: The dot (or square) beside each label is in the colour of the method that drew it — the chips above show which colour is which. VSA draws arrows instead.

volume.title: Volume (RVOL)
volume.info: Relative volume: how heavy this stock's recent trading is versus its own normal. It divides the average volume of the last few sessions by the typical (median) volume of the sessions before them, so one exceptional day such as a report does not distort the reference. 1.0× = a typical session; ~1.5–2× is elevated and ~3×+ is extreme — a sign of unusual professional interest. Same measure as the Volume surge page.
volume.noData: Not enough history to measure volume yet.

summary.title: Analytics summary
summary.info: The bottom line: StockPilot's separate opinions — the VSA verdict, the AI Insight second opinion, the Signal Trust Score and every trading method — pulled together into one read. The stance is the consolidated direction; 'agreement' is how strongly the signals line up (100 = unanimous, 50 = evenly split). Computed locally on the server; deterministic and free.
summary.disclaimer: {{engine}} · as of {{asOf}} · a summary of historical data, not investment advice

simulation.title: Trade simulation · VSA V4
simulation.info: Your VSA program (method VSA V4) replayed over this stock's stored history with its own trade simulator. Each time its sequence completes — a signal of strength, then a quiet test (No Supply or Test), then an up bar confirming that test — the simulated account buys at the next session's open, puts a stop under the sequence and a target three stop-distances away, and risks 1% of the account on the trade. One position at a time. Costs: 0.20% commission and 0.05% slippage each way. It shows how the rules would have played out here — not a forecast and not investment advice.
simulation.sidesLabel: Which setups the simulated account takes
simulation.skippedInfo: A confirmed setup is skipped when a position is already open (one at a time) or when the next open gaps through its stop.
simulation.noSetups: The program's sequence never completed on this stock's stored history, so there is nothing to simulate.
simulation.noTrades: None of the confirmed setups could be entered — a position was already open, or the next open gapped through the stop.
simulation.assumptions: {{risk}} of the account at risk per trade · target {{rr}}R · costs {{commission}} + {{slippage}} slippage each way · entry at the next open · {{from}} – {{to}} ({{bars}} sessions)
simulation.note: An educational replay of your program on past prices. R is a trade's result in units of its planned risk: −1R is a full stop, +3R the target. The account moves little because only 1% is risked per trade and it waits in cash between trades — compare the R figures, not the account with buy & hold.

legal.intro: StockPilot is a free, automated technical-analysis tool for companies listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange (GPW) and on selected foreign exchanges (NASDAQ, NYSE, Xetra, Euronext Paris, Euronext Amsterdam, London Stock Exchange). What follows describes what the ratings published here are — and are not — who is responsible for the site, and what data it processes.
legal.inlineNote: Automated technical analysis of historical data — this is not investment advice.
legal.footerNote: This site is informational and educational. The ratings shown are produced by automated technical analysis of historical data and are neither investment advice nor a personal recommendation. Investing carries the risk of losing your capital.
legal.footerLink: Legal information, terms of service and privacy policy

what.heading: What this site is
what.body: StockPilot analyses the historical price and volume data of the listed companies it covers using Volume Spread Analysis (VSA) and several other mechanical technical-analysis methods. The output is a numeric rating on a 0–100 scale plus a description of the pattern detected on the chart. The site is free to use.

method.heading: Methodology
method.body: Every rating is produced by the algorithms described in the Help section, from the open, close, high, low and volume of recent trading sessions. The analysis does not take into account company filings or periodic reports, inside information, or any source other than the market data named below. The historical signal effectiveness shown on the site comes from tests on past data and is no guarantee of future results.

meaning.heading: What the ratings mean
meaning.body: A high rating means only that the algorithm recognised a pattern historically associated with buyers being in control — it is not a recommendation to buy the instrument. A low rating means a pattern associated with sellers being in control and is not a recommendation to sell. The analysis horizon is a few to a few dozen trading sessions.

nature.heading: The nature of the information published
nature.body: The content published here is neither investment advice nor a personal recommendation within the meaning of the Polish Act of 29 July 2005 on Trading in Financial Instruments. It is addressed to an undefined audience and takes no account of the individual situation, knowledge, experience or investment objectives of any reader. It is also not an offer or an inducement to buy or sell any financial instrument.

risk.heading: Risk
risk.body: Investing in financial instruments carries the risk of losing part or all of the money invested. Share prices can move sharply. Investment decisions are yours alone, to be made after your own analysis and, where needed, after consulting a licensed investment adviser. The publisher accepts no liability for the consequences of decisions taken on the basis of this site.

sources.heading: Data sources
sources.body: Quotes come from Yahoo Finance and, as a fallback, from stooq.pl; the company financials shown come from the same sources. This is end-of-day historical data — not real-time data — and it may contain errors, gaps or delays. The publisher is not the source of this data, does not verify its accuracy and does not guarantee its completeness.

conflict.heading: Conflicts of interest
conflict.body: The publisher may hold positions in the companies shown on the site. The site is not sponsored by any issuer or financial-market institution and carries no advertising, paid placements or affiliate links. The ordering and the ratings of companies follow from the algorithm alone.

dating.heading: Dating of the ratings
dating.body: Every rating carries the date of the trading session it was computed for. Data refreshes automatically once a day after the close of each exchange. A rating computed earlier may no longer match the current state of the market.

scope.heading: 1. General provisions
scope.body: These terms govern the use of the StockPilot website at stocksignal.pl. The service provider is the entity named under “Site publisher”. Using the site means accepting these terms.

service.heading: 2. The service
service.body: The service consists of making the results of automated technical analysis of the listed companies it covers — the ranking, charts, signals and indicators — available electronically, free of charge. No registration or account is required. The agreement is concluded for a definite period and ends when you leave the site.

requirements.heading: 3. Technical requirements
requirements.body: You need an internet-connected device and a current browser with JavaScript and local storage (localStorage) enabled. Disabling local storage prevents your settings from being remembered but does not block access to the content.

rules.heading: 4. Rules of use
rules.body: Supplying unlawful content is prohibited, as is any action that disrupts the site — in particular automated bulk downloading of content (scraping), placing excessive load on the server, and circumventing technical limits. The content of the site may be used for your own personal purposes only.

availability.heading: 5. Availability
availability.body: The site is provided “as is”. The service provider does not guarantee uninterrupted availability, nor the completeness and accuracy of the data shown, and reserves the right to take the service down for maintenance and to change or discontinue it at any time.

liability.heading: 6. Liability
liability.body: The site is informational and educational. The service provider accepts no liability for investment decisions taken on the basis of its content, or for their financial consequences. See the “Legal disclaimer” section for details.

complaints.heading: 7. Complaints
complaints.body: Comments and complaints about the site can be sent to the email address given under “Site publisher”. Please describe the problem. A reply is sent to the sender's email address within 14 days.

changes.heading: 8. Changes to these terms
changes.body: The service provider may amend these terms; a new version takes effect when it is published on the site. The date of the last update is shown at the top of this page.

controller.heading: Data controller
controller.body: The controller of personal data processed in connection with your use of the site is the entity named under “Site publisher”. For data-protection matters, use the email address given above.

scope.heading: What data is processed
scope.body: Registration is optional. If you create an account, the server stores your account details and the items you save to it, including named filter presets. Server logs record the IP address, request time, resource requested, browser and operating-system type, and referring page.

purpose.heading: Purpose and legal basis
purpose.body: Log data is processed to keep the site secure, diagnose faults and prevent abuse, on the basis of the controller's legitimate interest (Article 6(1)(f) GDPR). It is not used for profiling or for marketing.

retention.heading: Retention
retention.body: Server logs are kept for as long as the purposes above require — typically no more than a few weeks — after which log rotation overwrites them automatically.

recipients.heading: Recipients
recipients.body: Data is not sold or passed to third parties for marketing. The hosting provider has access to the server infrastructure and acts as a processor. The site uses no analytics tools (such as Google Analytics), no advertising and no social-media plugins, so it passes no information about your visit to third parties.

storage.heading: Browser local storage
storage.body: Your browser remembers your theme, language, VSA settings, and any favourites and filter presets saved as a guest. Clearing site data removes those local copies. Presets you save while signed in, or choose to copy to your account, are stored on the server so you can use them on other devices. You can delete an account preset from the Filters page.

rights.heading: Your rights
rights.body: You have the right to access your data, to have it rectified, erased or its processing restricted, to object to processing, and to lodge a complaint with the President of the Personal Data Protection Office (UODO).

external.heading: External links
external.body: The site may link to external pages, for example to data sources or to material describing the analysis methods. The publisher is not responsible for the content or the privacy practices of those pages.

screenerFilters.priceChangeInfo: Change against the previous close for the latest available session, including live prices when available. Negative values find falling stocks. Different markets may show different sessions.
screenerFilters.volumeInfo: Upper limit on the 20-session median share volume. Works together with the existing minimum volume filter; this is not today's volume.
screenerFilters.scoreInfo: Mean score (0–100) of available active trading methods. Stocks without a score are excluded when a score bound is set.
screenerFilters.tradesInfo: Minimum number of reported open-market transactions in the selected reporting period. Buying and net buying count purchases; selling and net selling count sales; any activity counts both. This counts transactions, not distinct people.
screenerFilters.ageInfo: Maximum days between the latest matching transaction and the period end. Use 0 for transactions on the end date.
screenerFilters.value30Info: Minimum trade value in the 30 days through the period end. Uses purchase or sale amounts for one side, the balance in the selected direction for net filters, and total turnover for any activity.

insiderFilters.endInfo: Leave blank to use today. Trades on the end date are included.
insiderFilters.sortInfo: Purchases count as positive and sales as negative. Buying and selling show the selected side. Any activity and net filters show purchases minus sales. Ascending puts the most negative value first. Unknown values sort last.
insiderFilters.info: Reported open-market purchases and sales only. Net buying means purchase value exceeds sale value; net selling means the reverse. Grants, options, gifts and buybacks are excluded.
insiderFilters.periodInfo: Calendar days through the selected end date, inclusive. Uses the trade date, falling back to publication date when unavailable. The 30-day column uses the same end date.
insiderFilters.valueInfo: Minimum total purchase or sale value for the selected side. For net buying/selling, uses the absolute net value. With any activity, uses purchases plus sales. Foreign currencies use the app's indicative PLN rates. Unknown amounts do not meet value filters.
insiderFilters.coverage: Insider filters use stored public filings, refreshed daily. Missing filings do not prove there was no insider activity. Amounts use indicative PLN conversion rates; unknown values are excluded from value and net filters.

insider.loadError: Could not load insider transactions. Please try again.
insider.mixedCurrenciesNote: Transactions use different currencies. Overall totals show share counts; amounts by insider are separated by currency.
insider.gpwSourceNote: Source: ESPI reports and MAR Article 19 attachments. Covers recent available reports, not the complete transaction history.
insider.totalsScopeNote: Totals cover parsed transactions under the selected filter. Net shares are not the current holding. Missing values remain unknown; currencies are counted separately.
insider.title: Insider Buying & Selling
insider.info: Reported share transactions by executives, board directors, and closely associated persons (GPW ESPI MAR Art. 19 filings for Poland; SEC Form 4 / Yahoo Finance for US & UK). Plotted on the chart on the filing publication date (green marker below the bar = buy, red marker above the bar = sell).
insider.asymmetryNote: Signal asymmetry: insiders sell shares for many reasons (taxes, diversification, personal expenses), but buy on the open market with their own money for one reason — they expect the stock to rise.
insider.empty: No transactions were read for this filter. Check the data notes or refresh reports; no results do not prove there were no transactions.

fundamentals.title: Fundamental assessment
fundamentals.introduction: The new fundamental assessment covers profitability, growth, cash flow, debt and valuation. The ranking defaults to this assessment. The existing QVM score remains a separate measure.
fundamentals.methodology: Applicable pillars carry equal weights. Inputs compare companies with the same profile and market, preferring the same sector. Each metric needs at least 5 comparable companies. Profitability, cash flow and valuation need at least 2 metrics; growth and debt need 1. The overall score requires every applicable pillar. This is a relative screen, not a return forecast.
fundamentals.notApplicable: Not applicable to this profile: {{pillars}}. The remaining 3 pillars carry equal weights.
fundamentals.noneScored: No complete fundamental assessments. Expand a company to inspect available pillars and missing evidence. New inputs arrive with the next financial-data download.

portfolio.costHint: FIFO matches sales to the oldest purchases. Moving average allocates the cost of held shares proportionally. Buy fees increase the cost basis; sale fees reduce the realized result. Changing the method recalculates the portfolio’s entire history.
portfolio.priceHint: Position value is quantity × latest available price. Each quote shows its date and type. Quotes older than 7 days are flagged; this is an informational threshold, not an exchange calendar. Refreshing the page reads application data rather than requesting a new market quote.
portfolio.returnHint: The percentage result of an open position is unrealized profit or loss divided by remaining cost basis. It is not an annualized return or total account performance adjusted for deposits, withdrawals and currencies.
portfolio.scopeHint: Supports stock purchases and sales without short positions. A matching XTB Open Positions snapshot can set the Cash Operations holdings and costs on the report date. Trades through that snapshot are then locked. The combined value includes each saved wallet, including any separately imported XTB reports with overlapping holdings. Dividends, splits and taxes are excluded from trade history. This is not a tax report.
portfolio.editChanged: The portfolio changed while you were editing. Cancel and reopen the editor to use current data.
